event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: No bout among the 12 on the card was cancelled or changed during fight week; all 12 remain as listed. Weigh-ins (Fri Oct 30): Francis Marshall missed featherweight by 2 lb (148 vs 146 limit); the Hope bout is expected to proceed, likely at a catchweight with a purse forfeit, but that was unconfirmed when read. Everyone else posted made weight within the 1 lb non-title allowance. Ode Osbourne, Cody Durden, Nick Klein and Talita Alencar had no weight posted yet on UFC.com when read (pending, not reported misses). Earlier changes, all before fight week: Tom Nolan replaced the injured Brian Ortega in the main event (September); Dakota Hope replaced Gaston Bolanos (cut) vs Francis Marshall (Oct 8); Jacobe Smith replaced the injured Carlos Leal vs Randy Brown (about Oct 19). Azamat Bekoev vs Andre Petroski was scrapped on Oct 25-26 after Bekoev's anaphylactic reaction; Petroski declined a replacement and moved to UFC Vegas 124 (that bout is not in the 12-bout card list).

Short-notice replacement: unbeaten welterweight booked against Randy Brown after original opponent Carlos Leal withdrew injured; comes 28 days after his win over Bruce Whitehead.

Says he will 'be doing the dictating': plans to either wrestle Brown or finish him early depending on how the start goes; has not had a full camp for any of his four UFC fights. Targets a ranked opponent next and a title shot by early 2028.

Media day: calls the opponent switch a curveball, frames it as a must-win after losses to Kevin Holland and Gabriel Bonfim, says he has something Smith hasn't seen and wants to hurt and finish him ('The prediction is pain').
Opponent change: Gaston Bolanos withdrew after an eyebrow cut in training; Dakota Hope steps in.
Short-notice replacement for Gaston Bolanos (training cut) against Francis Marshall.

Says Nolan is more dangerous than Brian Ortega (the original opponent) and a win would do more for his resume; rejects Nolan's praise ('I don't want compliments, I want money'); stresses he only gets half his pay if he loses.

Has three fights left on his UFC deal, wants to fight it out and then test free agency; undecided on continuing beyond that. Wife expecting twins in December; runs his own promotion with an event on Dec 5.

First UFC main event and first five-rounder (stepped in after Ortega withdrew; Moicano pushed for five rounds). Studied Moicano's Saint Denis win and his body-triangle transitions; says he wants to win with ground and pound and elbows. Striking-first style.
Calls the fight a manifestation; questions Moicano's motivation and says if it becomes a battle of grit he will win it. No specific game plan given.

Camp change (pre-fight-week context): left Team Compton MMA in Australia to relocate to City Kickboxing (Eugene Bareman) in Auckland, bringing two teammates. This is his first fight out of that camp as far as reported.

Announces this is his retirement fight win or lose (health, young child). Would like to finish Lee by submission off his wrestling/grappling but will trade if it goes that way; expects Lee to stand and bang.
Enters on a two-fight losing streak and is described as possibly fighting for his UFC spot.
Says he had a hard camp and feels great; respects Lebosnoyani's jiu-jitsu and striking; promises a better show after his 17-takedown decision debut. No injuries mentioned.
Studied Hasanov's tape, impressed by his wrestling and explosiveness; game plan built to neutralise those strengths. Wants to go 3-0 in the UFC and is not chasing big jumps.
On a four-fight losing skid (no win since July 2021) and moving up from welterweight to middleweight for this bout.
